briefing:
SITUATION BRIEFING — Round 2

It is Day 1, 10:00 CET. Russia has seized a narrow corridor through the Suwałki Gap approximately 6 hours ago.

MILITARY: Russian forces hold a ~15km wide corridor connecting Kaliningrad to Belarus through Lithuanian territory. 3 BTGs from Kaliningrad (north) and 2 BTGs from Western District via Belarus (south-east) are consolidating positions. Key Route 16/E67 junction at Mockava held by Spetsnaz. GPS jamming active. Lithuanian border guards have withdrawn. The German EFP battlegroup at Rukla is on full alert but has NOT engaged — awaiting NATO orders. Polish forces along the southern border are at highest readiness. US V Corps at Camp Kościuszko is mobilizing.

CYBER: Lithuanian military C2 degraded to ~60% effectiveness. Civilian comms disrupted across Suwałki region. NATO SATCOM links unaffected.

DIPLOMATIC: Lithuania has invoked Article 4. NAC emergency session convening in 2 hours. Russia claims 'humanitarian corridor' with 'no territorial claims.' No shots fired at NATO forces yet — Russia is carefully avoiding a direct NATO engagement.

GLOBAL REACTIONS: Still forming. Most capitals woke up to the news between 05:00-07:00 CET. UN Security Council emergency session requested by Lithuania and Poland.

CRITICAL: Russia has NOT fired on any NATO troops. The EFP battlegroup in Lithuania is untouched. This is deliberate — Moscow wants to present the corridor as a fait accompli before NATO can formulate a unified response.
narrative:
At 03:47 CET on Day 1, the Suwałki Crisis began — not with a dramatic declaration but with a carefully choreographed fait accompli. Three Russian Battalion Tactical Groups from the Kaliningrad garrison, supported by elements of the Baltic Fleet's Naval Infantry, crossed into the Suwałki Corridor from the north under cover of darkness and heavy electronic warfare jamming. Simultaneously, two BTGs from the Russian Western Military District entered Lithuanian territory from Belarus, advancing west toward the corridor. Belarus provided transit rights but — critically — did not commit its own forces, with Lukashenko telling his defense council that 'this is Russia's operation, not ours.'

The operation was preceded by 90 minutes of intense cyber attacks against Lithuanian communications infrastructure, degrading military C2 and civilian networks. GPS jamming blanketed the corridor. Russian Special Forces (Spetsnaz) seized the key Route 16/E67 junction at Mockava and two minor border crossings. By 06:00, Russian forces had advanced approximately 15km into the corridor, establishing a narrow land bridge between Kaliningrad and Belarus — severing the only land connection between the Baltic states and the rest of NATO.

The German-led NATO Enhanced Forward Presence battlegroup in Lithuania, positioned near Rukla (80km north of the corridor), received fragmentary intelligence of the incursion at 04:15 but could not confirm due to communications degradation. The first confirmed contact came at 04:52 when a Lithuanian border guard patrol at Kalvarija reported Russian armored vehicles crossing the border. Lithuania's President declared a state of emergency at 05:30 and formally invoked NATO Article 4 (consultation) at 05:45.

In Moscow, the Kremlin framed the operation as a 'humanitarian logistics corridor' to relieve Kaliningrad from what it called 'illegal NATO economic pressure.' Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Zakharova stated that Russia had 'no territorial claims' and that the corridor was 'temporary and limited.' Western intelligence agencies assessed this as standard Russian information warfare — the operation had clearly been planned for months.
